messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw a spike in vanity tenant pages this morning, SLOs fired a bunch of simultaneous alerts. Thinking we should try a tiered dampening strategy rather than global silence.
kevin: ugh, yeah saw the flood. Can you paste an example of the signal? is it request_latency p95 or error_rate?
alex: mostly p95 latency (frontend route). Error rate stayed low. Rough sample: `{"tenant": "vanity-inc", "p95_ms": 1200, "baseline_p95_ms": 200}`
ritika: If it's big tenant-driven bursts, global notify-suppression is too blunt. Proposal: per-tenant short backoff windows + exponential cooldown on re-alerts.
eva: +1. Also add a percentile-bucket check so we don't suppress genuine regressions across many tenants. For example: if p95 increases for >50% of tenants, skip dampening.
kevin: That matches my thinking. Implementation question: do we encode this as routing policy rules in the console or as API-level flags on the alerts engine?
alex: two parts: 1) a console UI to express the intent (dampening tiers, percentile overrides) 2) API payload that the alerts engine consumes. So users can preview the policy in console before rollout.
tom_p: UX note: preview needs clear explainers — what suppressed, why, and a time slider. People will debug missing pages otherwise.
ritika: Agree. Also want a quick toggle to force notify for a tenant during incident postmortems. Maybe a per-tenant "bypass" flag.
kevin: On schema: thinking something like: 
```json
{"policy_id": "tiered-dampener-v1", "scopes": ["tenant"], "rules": [{"threshold": {"metric": "p95_latency", "op": ">", "value": 500}, "dampening": {"initial_backoff_s": 60, "multiplier": 2, "max_backoff_s": 3600}}], "percentile_override": {"window_mins": 15, "tenant_percentile": 0.5} }
```
alex: That looks good. Need to ensure the console presents these fields in human terms — e.g., "Initial quiet period", "Backoff factor" etc.
eva: Telemetry: we should surface two things in dashboards — suppressed_alert_count and suppressed_latency_impact (approx tokens/savings equivalent). Helps justify the dampening.
tom_p: Also show a simulated alert stream when user adjusts parameters (what would have been suppressed historically). That sells the feature.
ritika: For rollout: start as opt-in on a small set of tenants, run for 48h, then auto-suggest for other tenants with similar traffic patterns.
eva: One more: tie into routing policies so that suppressed alerts can still trigger lower-severity channels (e.g., #ops-monitoring vs oncall pager) — gradation rather than silence.
alex: Good point. Implementation note: alerts engine should emit a suppressed event with metadata: reason, original_severity, suppressed_to_severity. Console can map channels by severity.
kevin: Any security/data concerns if we surface per-tenant p95 in the public console? For multi-tenant customers we need to mask tenant ids unless allowed.
tom_p: We can show anonymized tenant cohorts and allow explicit allowlist for showing names.
ritika: Tasks: 1) draft API schema PR for policy payload (kevin) 2) console preview mockups (tom_p + eva) 3) telemetry metrics spec (eva) 4) rollout plan + experiments (alex + ritika).
kevin: I'll open the PR and link a rough API contract by EOD.
alex: thanks — tagging @devops-bot to kick off an experimental job that replays last 30 days for the new policy so UX can simulate.
devops-bot: scheduled replay job 38291 for policy-sim, ETA 2h. Logs will be posted to #eng-platform once complete. :robot_face:
eva: awesome. Once we have replay data, I can prototype the simulated timeline in the console.
ritika: +1. Also adding a tiny checkbox in the policy UI: "route suppressed alerts to degraded-channel".
alex: sweet. We'll reconvene after replay results. :thumbsup:
